title: Python: resolveStarAttribute picks the last of two conditional stars alone: m.f() gives b.f where Python allows a.f or b.f (split from GCLI-125)
description: Split out of GCLI-125 by the leader's ruling (do not widen GCLI-125). WRONG edges in the attribute form, from resolveStarAttribute (src/python/calls.ts), which walks a holder's stars last to first and ignores whether a star may be skipped (the known gap its doc comment names), so the last complete star that exports the name decides alone. It decides whenever moduleBindingGate returns null: m has no def, class or import of the name. Input 1: a.py and b.py each def f; m.py is 'try: from a import *' / 'except ImportError: from b import *'; app.py 'import m; m.f()'. origin/dev (3d3986b) gives ONE unflagged edge to b.f; Python allows a.f or b.f. Input 2 (Opus round 1 on opum-ai/glyph-cli#202): x.py and y.py each def f; m.py is 'from y import *' then 'if C:' with 'from x import *' inside; app.py 'import m; m.f()'. dev and #202 give ONE unflagged edge to x.f; Python allows y.f or x.f. The bare form 'from m import f; f()' is already right for both inputs: it gives both alternatives, each multiplyBound. A single unflagged edge where Python allows two is wrong under DEC-303 (a10) Q2 and (a43) item 2. Fix shape: a deciding star that may be skipped (the maySkipStatement rule, as GCLI-125 records on the module scope in starMaySkipLines) is the star's symbols plus what an earlier star decides, each multiplyBound, or a refusal when an earlier star is partial; the same rule GCLI-125 applies in starOverride. Wrong-edge class: for opum-doc's (a49) item 7 hold-list decision.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the reproducing input gives alternatives each multiplyBound or no edge, never b.f alone, red before and green after, with callees pinned and the full bin delta
twins: a single unconditional star keeps deciding alone; a conditional lone star keeps deciding (it is the only way the name binds)
a mutant that restores the last-star-decides rule is observed red
the five-pin corpus diff against dev is script-asserted with every moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear
